name: ELEGOO Smart Robot Car Kit V4
description: An Arduino Uno-compatible, 4WD skid-steer car kit — the true beginner's entry point in this subcategory, at roughly a third of the price of anything else built here so far. No Raspberry Pi, no Python, no ROS: it's programmed in Arduino C/C++, drives by differential wheel speed rather than Ackermann or mecanum steering, and its bundled ESP32 camera streams raw FPV video for phone-based driving rather than running any onboard computer vision.

sourcing: Verified against ELEGOO's official V4.0 (With Camera) product pages (US and EU storefronts) and its official V4.0 and legacy V3.0/V2.0/V1.0 tutorial blog posts; ELEGOO's "About" page; its official GitHub repository for this kit, including its archived status, lack of a license file, and an unanswered licensing issue; Amazon and Micro Center listings; independent reviews from Teach Your Kids Code and The New Stack; an Arduino Forum troubleshooting thread on a common power-related failure mode; and ELEGOO's aggregate Trustpilot rating. Flagged as uncertain: exact current Amazon review volume and star rating (not independently retrievable at research time); and whether every currently-sold V4.0 unit ships with the ESP32 camera bundled by default, since ELEGOO has at points sold camera-less and camera-equipped variants under overlapping naming — this catalog's photo and specs describe the camera-equipped configuration.

pricing.summary: ELEGOO's own store lists the V4.0 (With Camera) kit at $75.99, the lowest price in this subcategory, and it's also sold on Amazon, Micro Center, and other resellers. A screwdriver and tools are included, but 18650 battery cells are not, so the car can't run until batteries are sourced separately.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The Smart Robot Car Kit V4.0 has the weakest open-source story in this subcategory: ELEGOO's GitHub repo ships zipped code with no license file, an unanswered licensing question, and is now archived, so no Open Source badge is applied here.

firmwareCommunity.note: ELEGOO's own GitHub repo for this kit ships code as zipped downloads with no license file and is now archived, so most ongoing development activity happens in third-party community forks instead.
